question: EIC Pathfinder Challenges call:

options.A: Builds on new, cutting-edge directions in science and technology
options.B: Aims to disrupt a market or to create new opportunities by realising innovative technological solutions, grounded in high-risk/high-gain research and development
options.C: Establishes a portfolio of projects for each Challenge that explores different perspectives, competing approaches or complementary aspects of a predefined thematic area
options.D: Proactively managed by EIC Programme Managers

title: General Overview
answerText: All of the above.

question: When evaluating a proposal my reference document(s) is (are):

options.A: The proposal template
options.B: The Work Programme and the Challenge guide
options.C: Both A) and B)

title: General Overview
answerText: The Work Programme and the Challenge guide

question: An Individual Evaluator’s tasks include:

options.A: Drafting Individual Evaluation Report (IER)
options.B: Drafting Consensus Report (CR)
options.C: Approving CR

title: General Overview
answerText: Both A) and C)

question: Which of the following is allowed by the Confidentiality clause:

options.A: Discuss evaluation matters with EU staff not involved in the evaluation
options.B: Contact partners in the consortium, sub-contractors or any third parties
options.C: Disclose names of your fellow experts.
options.D: Discuss evaluation matters with your fellow experts who are evaluating the same proposal in a consensus group or Panel review.

title: General Overview
answerText: Discuss evaluation matters with your fellow experts who are evaluating the same proposal in a consensus group or Panel review.

question: Which of the following is NOT true with respect to the use of generative AI in proposal preparation:

options.A: It is not allowed
options.B: It is allowed, but the applicants must verify the accuracy, validity, and appropriateness of the content and any citations generated by the AI tool and correct any errors or inconsistencies.
options.C: It is allowed, but the applicants must provide a list of sources used to generate content and citations, including those generated by the AI tool. Double-check citations to ensure they are accurate and properly referenced.
options.D: It is allowed, but the applicants must be conscious of the potential for plagiarism where the AI tool may have reproduced substantial text from other sources. Check the original sources to be sure you are not plagiarising someone else’s work.
options.E: It is allowed, but the applicants must acknowledge the limitations of the AI tool in the proposal preparation, including the potential for bias, errors, and gaps in knowledge.

title: General Overview
answerText: It is not allowed

question: Which of the following represent a possible Conflict of Interest (CoI) at proposal level (note: not exhaustive!):

options.A: I have collaborated in a research project with one of the applicants in 2021
options.B: I have published with one of the applicants in the past 3 years
options.C: I have heard of one of the applicants

title: General Overview
answerText: I have published with one of the applicants in the past 3 years

question: I am automatically in a Conflict of Interest (CoI) at evaluation level if (note: not exhaustive!):

options.A: I am a director or trustee of the applicant
options.B: I have contributed to the drafting of a proposal submitted to the call
options.C: I am a National Contact Point
options.D: I am in one or more of the above cases

title: General Overview
answerText: I am in one or more of the above cases

question: If I find out I might have a potential conflict of interest:

options.A: I flag this immediately to the Call Coordinator
options.B: I decline the assignment immediately
options.C: I continue with the evaluation as it is not my role to highlight it

title: General Overview
answerText: I decline the assignment immediately

question: The Evaluation Workflow consists of:

options.A: Drafting IERs and quality check
options.B: Creating CR and reaching consensus
options.C: Cross reading and confirming the comments and scores

title: General Overview
answerText: All A), B), and C)

question: Which organisations are NOT exempt from the assessment of their Operational capacity in terms of know-how, qualifications and resources to successfully implement their tasks:

options.A: Public bodies
options.B: Member State organisations
options.C: International organisations

title: General Overview
answerText: SMEs and big corporations

question: When evaluating the quality of open science practices of a proposal I should:

options.A: Verify if all publications mentioned in the bibliographic reference are openly accessible
options.B: Consider if the consortium plans to provide open access to all publication generated by the project and plans to manage digital data according to the FAIR principles
options.C: Exclude research data management
options.D: Disregard involvement of additional knowledge actors, like citizens, civil society, and end users.

title: General Overview
answerText: Consider if the consortium plans to provide open access to all publication generated by the project and plans to manage digital data according to the FAIR principles

question: Which statement with respect to aspects and measures related to intellectual property protection and to exploitation is NOT correct:

options.A: It should be comprehensive and feasible and should include protection measures whenever relevant.
options.B: It should be commensurate with the described pathways to outcomes and impacts and therefore underpins the ‘credibility’ of these pathways.
options.C: It should consider ‘freedom to operate’ regarding the background owned by consortium members and/or third parties outside the consortium.
options.D: Should give due thought to balancing between publication of results and plans to protect IP, e.g. in terms of timing the respective activities, involvement of IP experts.
options.E: The exploitation is expected only in Member states or Associated countries.

title: General Overview
answerText: The exploitation is expected only in Member states or Associated countries.

question: The gender dimension of a proposal:

options.A: Refers to gender balance in the consortium’s teams.
options.B: Refers to the project’s research and innovation content.
options.C: Is not evaluated under Excellence.

title: General Overview
answerText: Refers to the project’s research and innovation content.

question: The composition of the consortium submitting a proposal is eligible if:

options.A: It consists of a single legal entity established in a Member State or an Associated Country (unless stated otherwise in the specific Challenge chapter).
options.B: It comprises two independent legal entities from two different Member States or Associated Countries.
options.C: It comprises three or more independent legal entities, such that at least one is from a Member State and at least two more are from two other different Member States or Associated Countries.

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Any one of the above.

question: What is a good sequence of actions, when starting to evaluate a proposal:

options.A: Check potential CoI, check if you have relevant expertise, accept the assignment, check if the proposal is in/out of scope, evaluate according to the Award criteria, answer the additional questions
options.B: Accept the assignment, check potential CoI, check if you have relevant expertise, accept the assignment, check if the proposal is in/out of scope, answer the additional questions, evaluate according to the Award criteria
options.C: Check potential CoI, accept the assignment, check if the proposal is in/out of scope, answer the additional questions, evaluate according to the Award criteria, check if you have relevant expertise
options.D: Check if you have relevant expertise, accept the assignment, check potential CoI, evaluate according to the Award criteria, check if the proposal is in/out of scope, answer the additional questions

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Check potential CoI, check if you have relevant expertise, accept the assignment, check if the proposal is in/out of scope, evaluate according to the Award criteria, answer the additional questions

question: The How many award criteria are there for the evaluation of Pathfinder Challenges?
title: Guidance for IER and CR

question: Which is the most important award criterion in the Pathfinder Challenge evaluation weighting 50% of the total score:

options.A: Impact
options.B: Excellence
options.C: Quality and efficiency of the implementation

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Excellence

question: When I define scores for a given award criterion:

options.A: I should not give 5 (excellent) to a proposal which successfully addresses all relevant aspects of the award criterion but present a minor shortcoming
options.B: The whole range of scores (0-5) should be used
options.C: Half-marks cannot be used

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: The whole range of scores (0-5) should be used

question: If a proposal fails to discuss a sub-criterion:

options.A: I do not evaluate that criterion at all and score accordingly
options.B: I evaluate the other sub-criteria under the respective criterion and score accordingly penalizing for the missing sub criterion
options.C: None of the above

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: I evaluate the other sub-criteria under the respective criterion and score accordingly penalizing for the missing sub criterion

question: When giving my assessment, the scores should clearly reflect:

options.A: Shortcoming, weaknesses, and strengths identified in the comments
options.B: Shortcomings and weaknesses
options.C: Only strengths

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Shortcoming, weaknesses, and strengths identified in the comments

question: A Pathfinder Challenge proposal must:

options.A: Address the specific requirements of the challenge it is submitted to
options.B: Target a technological breakthrough
options.C: Have a TRL between 5 and 6

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Address the specific requirements of the challenge it is submitted to

question: When evaluating the plausibility of the methodology I should:

options.A: Penalise a proposal that in my opinion is not feasible in the proposed timeframe
options.B: Provide a high score to a proposal that presents a good interconnection among the work packages and a coherent timeline to deliver the expected deliverables/milestones
options.C: Positively judge a proposal that presents a sound methodology, e.g., it founds on preliminary data and uses appropriate methods to prove their hypothesis

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Positively judge a proposal that presents a sound methodology, e.g., it founds on preliminary data and uses appropriate methods to prove their hypothesis

question: I assess gender balance:

options.A: In criterion implementation
options.B: In criterion excellence
options.C: Nowhere as it is not an evaluation criterion

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Nowhere as it is not an evaluation criterion

question: If the proposal does not mention how to achieve the expected outcomes, nor mentions the impact on the challenge, I:

options.A: Contact the Call Coordinator in order to get such information from the applicant
options.B: Evaluate the proposal without considering this missing part
options.C: Comment and penalise, in a proportioned manner, in the Impact criterion because of this missing information

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Comment and penalise, in a proportioned manner, in the Impact criterion because of this missing information

question: A proposal should indicate:

options.A: Adequate measures to protect their results for future exploitation
options.B: Proposed measures to involve and empower key actors that have the potential to translate research into innovations
options.C: Both A) and B)

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Both A) and B)

question: A detailed plan for exploitation and dissemination of results including communication activities is not included in the proposal I am evaluating:

options.A: It is a weakness since the detailed plan is mandatory at proposal stage. I will comment accordingly and reflect this aspect with a lower score
options.B: A detailed plan is not mandatory at proposal stage. I evaluate the plan based on the information provided
options.C: It depends on the duration of the project: the detailed plan is mandatory only if the duration is more than 30 months. My comment will consider the specificity of this requirement

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: A detailed plan is not mandatory at proposal stage. I evaluate the plan based on the information provided

question: In the proposal I am evaluating, some target groups for the communication and dissemination measure are identified, but in my opinion other important ones are missing:

options.A: The consortium can decide which target groups they will address; therefore, I do not penalise the proposal nor comment on the missing groups
options.B: I formulate my comment and appropriately penalise the proposal clarifying that some target groups have not been duly considered
options.C: I formulate my comment suggesting to specifically consider some target groups in case the proposal will be resubmitted since this would be extremely beneficial for the proposal

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: I formulate my comment and appropriately penalise the proposal clarifying that some target groups have not been duly considered

question: The work plan details (e.g. risk mitigation plan) must be evaluated under:

options.A: Excellence criterion - plausibility of the methodology
options.B: Quality and efficiency of the implementation – work plan
options.C: Both excellence and quality and efficiency of the implementation criteria

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Quality and efficiency of the implementation – work plan

question: When looking at the “allocation of resources” sub-criterion, I should (multiple choice possible):

options.A: Assess the extent to which the consortium members have all the necessary high-quality expertise for performing the project tasks
options.B: Assess the appropriateness and effectiveness of the allocation of staff resources to work packages and consortium members
options.C: Penalise proposals that show expensive person-months
options.D: Assess the resources to be committed in terms of person-months and other cost items

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Assess the appropriateness and effectiveness of the allocation of staff resources to work packages and consortium members
Assess the resources to be committed in terms of person-months and other cost items

question: What type of comments should be avoided?

options.A: Specific to the relevant criterion addressing each sub-criterion
options.B: Of adequate length, assessing weaknesses, shortcomings and strengths
options.C: Not related to the criterion in question or with references to the same weakness under different criteria
options.D: Consisting of full sentences instead of bullet points

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Not related to the criterion in question or with references to the same weakness under different criteria

question: When drafting an Individual Evaluation Report, what elements are acceptable:

options.A: Citations and web links.
options.B: Suggestions for improvement of the proposal
options.C: Speculative expressions such as “seems to be” and “is difficult to see”
options.D: Making any reference to specific locations (ex. Page 15 of the proposal)

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: None of the above.

question: When working on reaching consensus, what is NOT the correct behaviour:

options.A: Engage in the discussion actively using SEP comments
options.B: Pay attention to comments of the VCR and other experts and respond in timely fashion
options.C: Be respectful, open-minded, flexible and take on board the comments of the other Evaluators
options.D: Do not change your mind and make sure you impose your views about the proposal
options.E: Make a best effort to reach consensus during the SEP process

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Do not change your mind and make sure you impose your views about the proposal

question: In SEP you will NOT be able to do the following:

options.A: Draft your Individual Evaluation Report
options.B: Submit your cost claim
options.C: Participate in an online consensus discussion
options.E: Find the documents relevant for each proposal

title: Guidance for IER and CR
answerText: Submit your cost claim

question: If you consider that a proposal is “out of scope”, you have to:

options.A: Declare the proposal to be “out of scope” and stop evaluating
options.B: Declare the proposal to be “out of scope” and evaluate it completely
options.C: Suggest changes, which would make the proposal “in scope”
options.D: Evaluate the proposal ignoring the issue, because anyway the score will be low

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Declare the proposal to be “out of scope” and evaluate it completely

question: If I realise that a consortium includes one participant requesting EU funding, based in a country that is neither an EU Member State nor associated to Horizon Europe nor low/middle income country (listed in the HORIZON EUROPE Work Programme):

options.A: I inform the Call Coordinator immediately as the so called third countries can participate to HORIZON EUROPE, but they cannot receive EU funding.
options.B: I must judge if its participation is essential for implementing the project (e.g., for example in view of its 1. outstanding competence/expertise, 2. access to particular research infrastructures, 3. access to particular geographical environments and 4. access to particular data) and record my comment in the “Exceptional Funding” box in SEP
options.C: I assume at the end they will provide their own funding and continue the evaluation without any comment

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: I must judge if its participation is essential for implementing the project (e.g., for example in view of its 1. outstanding competence/expertise, 2. access to particular research infrastructures, 3. access to particular geographical environments and 4. access to particular data) and record my comment in the “Exceptional Funding” box in SEP

question: If a UK entity participates in a proposal and requests EU funding, what shall I do?

options.A: Nothing as UK is an associated country to Horizon Europe
options.B: I provide an assessment in the additional question for “Exceptional Funding” because it is a third country
options.C: I don’t know

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Nothing as UK is an associated country to Horizon Europe

question: If a Swiss entity participates in a proposal and requests EU funding, what shall I do?

options.A: I consider it as an Associated Country and it is automatically eligible to receive EU funding
options.B: I provide an assessment in the additional question for “Exceptional Funding” because Switzerland is a third country
options.C: I don t know

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: I consider it as an Associated Country and it is automatically eligible to receive EU funding

question: A proposal uses human embryonic stem cells. What should you do?

options.A: Continue the evaluation considering removal of these activities, and comment these issues in the additional questions
options.B: Judge whether the use of hESC is or is not necessary to achieve the scientific objectives of the proposal and the reasons why.
options.C: Stop the evaluation of the proposal, as it will become ineligible
options.D: Inform the Call Coordinator who will decide on the way to proceed with the proposal

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Judge whether the use of hESC is or is not necessary to achieve the scientific objectives of the proposal and the reasons why.

question: The detailed lump sum budget table is evaluated under the section:

options.A: Excellence
options.B: Impact
options.C: Quality and efficiency of the implementation

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Quality and efficiency of the implementation

question: If the Lump sum budget has substantial weaknesses, e.g., in terms of structure and allocation of person-months and personnel cost, you must:

options.A: Provide comments under Quality and efficiency of the implementation and reduce the score accordingly
options.B: Do not penalise but suggest different structure of the budget
options.C: Assume the project will fix the weaknesses, if selected for funding, and only mention the issue in the Overall comments

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Provide comments under Quality and efficiency of the implementation and reduce the score accordingly

question: If the Lump sum budget is well organised and the allocation of resources (comprising person-months and other cost items) to work packages and consortium members is appropriate and effective, however you consider that there are factual errors in the budget allocated to big items or in personnel cost, you must:

options.A: Reduce the score on Quality and efficiency of the implementation
options.B: Provide precise budget recommendations with arguments for a reduction or reallocation in the Overall comments
options.C: Suggest modifications under Quality and efficiency of the implementation, without reducing the score

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Provide precise budget recommendations with arguments for a reduction or reallocation in the Overall comments

question: Recommendations on the lump sum detailed budget table should describe (choose the right answer(s)):

options.A: What are the changes proposed
options.B: Why a cost estimation should be changed
options.C: Why the allocation of resources should be changed (if applicable)

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: All of the above

question: For the assessment of personnel costs in the Budget table the evaluators:

options.A: Must use information from the relevant dashboard
options.B: Could use their previous experience as researchers.
options.C: Could use their previous experience as evaluators.
options.D: Should compare relevant information on the internet against the EU dashboard.

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Must use information from the relevant dashboard

question: In the lump sum assessment, the Individual Evaluators may not:

options.A: Recommend an increase of the total requested grant amount
options.B: Recommend a reduction of the lump sum amounts
options.C: Recommend a reallocation of certain items of the lump sum

title: Additional Questions and Lump Sum Budget
answerText: Recommend an increase of the total requested grant amount

question: When you receive the “Approve IER” task after an IER is submitted by an evaluator on the next day after starting the evaluation, you will

options.A: Disapprove the task to reopen immediately the IER, because the evaluator did not spend enough time assessing the proposal
options.B: Read carefully the IER and disapprove, even just for an inappropriate language
options.C: Start drafting the CR
options.D: Read carefully, and only in exceptional cases, like text in the IER, which is not relevant to the proposal or very limited and misplaced assessment, disapprove after providing your request for modifications in the Task comment field.

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Read carefully, and only in exceptional cases, like text in the IER, which is not relevant to the proposal or very limited and misplaced assessment, disapprove after providing your request for modifications in the Task comment field.

question: On a proposal, for which you are a Vice Chair, three days after disapproving a submitted IER, it still has not been resubmitted. In that case:

options.A: You inform the Challenge PO
options.B: You inform the Call Coordinator
options.C: You enter a comment in the Task comments field of the “Approve IER” task, encouraging the evaluator to implement your request and to submit.

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: You inform the Challenge PO

question: After receiving the three IERs and you are satisfied with their quality, you draft the CR by making sure:

options.A: It contains all the text from the three IERs.
options.B: It is a summary of the three IERs and contains specific opinions from different IERs only if they are contradictory and cannot be reconciled without a discussion
options.C: You include in the CR what you believe is the correct assessment.
options.D: You make a random choice from contradictory opinions and hope the evaluators will agree anyway
options.E: You re-evaluate the proposal and draft the CR from scratch.

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: It is a summary of the three IERs and contains specific opinions from different IERs only if they are contradictory and cannot be reconciled without a discussion

question: If a Swiss and UK entities participate in a proposal and requests EU funding, and if some of the evaluators have provided assessment concerning “Exceptional Funding”, what shall I do?

options.A: I consider them as Associated Countries, so they are automatically eligible to receive EU funding. I do not include in the CR any comments
options.B: I summarise in the CR the assessment from the evaluators in the additional question for “Exceptional Funding” because they are third countries, not directly eligible for funding
options.C: I include in the CR without modification any comments the evaluators may have provided
options.D: I disapprove the IERs for the evaluators who have not provided any comments

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: I consider them as Associated Countries, so they are automatically eligible to receive EU funding. I do not include in the CR any comments

question: A proposal uses human embryonic stem cells. What should you include in the CR?

options.A: Consider removal of these activities and draft a summary comment on these issues in the additional questions
options.B: Include a summary of the judgement by the individual evaluators whether the use of hESC is or is not necessary to achieve the scientific objectives of the proposal and the reasons why
options.C: Stop the drafting of the CR, as the proposal will become ineligible
options.D: Inform the Call Coordinator who will decide on the way to proceed with the proposal

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Include a summary of the judgement by the individual evaluators whether the use of hESC is or is not necessary to achieve the scientific objectives of the proposal and the reasons why

question: If the Lump sum budget has substantial weaknesses, e.g., in terms of structure and allocation of person-months and personnel cost, in the CR you must:

options.A: Provide comments under Quality and efficiency of the implementation and reduce the score accordingly
options.B: Do not penalise but suggest different structure of the budget
options.C: Assume the project will fix the weaknesses, if selected for funding, and only mention the issue in the Overall comments

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Provide comments under Quality and efficiency of the implementation and reduce the score accordingly

question: If the Lump sum budget is well organised and the allocation of resources (comprising person-months and other cost items) to work packages and consortium members is appropriate and effective, however some evaluators consider that there are factual errors in the budget allocated to big items or to personnel cost, in the CR you must:

options.A: Make sure the score on Quality and efficiency of the implementation is reduced
options.B: Include the precise budget recommendations from evaluators with arguments for a reduction or reallocation in the Overall comments
options.C: Include in the CR suggested modifications under Quality and efficiency of the implementation, without reducing the score

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Include the precise budget recommendations from evaluators with arguments for a reduction or reallocation in the Overall comments

question: Recommendations in the Overall comments on the lump sum detailed budget table should describe (choose the right answer(s)):

options.A: What are the changes proposed
options.B: Why a cost estimation should be changed
options.C: Why the allocation of resources should be changed (if applicable)

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: All of the above

question: In the lump sum assessment, in the CR there may not be:

options.A: A recommendation to increase of the total requested grant amount
options.B: A recommendation for a reduction of the lump sum amounts
options.C: A recommendation for a reallocation of certain items of the lump sum

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: A recommendation to increase of the total requested grant amount

question: In the CR, what type of comments should be avoided?

options.A: Specific to the relevant criterion addressing each sub-criterion;
options.B: Of adequate length, assessing weaknesses, shortcomings and strengths;
options.C: Not related to the criterion in question or with references to the same weakness under different criteria;
options.D: Consisting of full sentences instead of bullet points;

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Not related to the criterion in question or with references to the same weakness under different criteria;

question: When drafting the CR, what elements are acceptable:

options.A: Citations and web links.
options.B: Suggestions for improvement of the proposal.
options.C: Speculative expressions such as “seems to be” and “is difficult to see”.
options.D: Making any reference to specific locations (ex. Page 15 of the proposal).

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: None of the above.

question: After making the CR available to the evaluators for a consensus discussion, what is the follow up action:

options.A: Wait for the evaluators to reach consensus, without interfering at all
options.B: Moderate the discussion discretely, making sure it does not stall, and it does not become confrontational
options.C: Actively suggest who is the next to comment and do not allow for a too long free-flowing discussion
options.D: Explain that the CR you have created is perfect and there is nothing to discuss

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Moderate the discussion discretely, making sure it does not stall, and it does not become confrontational

question: When the evaluators discuss the score for a given award criterion:

options.A: They should not give 5 (excellent) to a proposal which successfully addresses all relevant aspects of the award criterion but present a minor shortcoming
options.B: The whole range of scores (0-5) should be used
options.C: Half-marks cannot be used

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: The whole range of scores (0-5) should be used

question: What is the requirement the scores should NOT definitely satisfy:

options.A: Correspond to the comments
options.B: From score 3 and above, in the assessment of the criterion there should be only shortcomings and not weaknesses
options.C: All should be above the corresponding thresholds
options.D: The application of the scoring scale should be coherent across the three criteria – same score for the same type of comments

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: All should be above the corresponding thresholds

question: What is the next step after all evaluators declare agreement with the current version of the CR, including the scores:

options.A: Submit the “Write CR” task to open the “Approve CR” task
options.B: Reopen the discussion, because you disagree with some of the comments
options.C: Inform the PO, so that the quality can be checked before submitting the “Write CR” task. If the PO approves, submit the “Write CR” task to open the “Approve CR” task
options.D: Suggest increasing the scores, because you like the proposal

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: Inform the PO, so that the quality can be checked before submitting the “Write CR” task. If the PO approves, submit the “Write CR” task to open the “Approve CR” task

question: If an online consensus meeting is organised, your role is:

options.A: To participate in the discussion on equal footing with the Individual evaluators
options.B: To take notes and after the meeting to draft a Consensus report
options.C: There is nothing for you to do
options.D: To modify the original CR in front of the participants according to the discussion to reflect the agreed points.

title: Vice Chairs Rapporteurs
answerText: To modify the original CR in front of the participants according to the discussion to reflect the agreed points.

question: EIC Pathfinder Challenges call:

options.A: Builds on new, cutting-edge directions in science and technology
options.B: Aims to disrupt a market or to create new opportunities by realising innovative technological solutions, grounded in high-risk/high-gain research and development
options.C: Establishes a portfolio of projects for each Challenge that explores different perspectives, competing approaches or complementary aspects of a predefined thematic area
options.D: Proactively managed by EIC Programme Managers

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: All of the above.

question: When evaluating a proposal my reference document(s) is (are):

options.A: The proposal template
options.B: The Work Programme and the Challenge guide
options.C: Both A) and B)

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: The Work Programme and the Challenge guide

question: An Individual Evaluator’s tasks include:

options.A: Drafting Individual Evaluation Report (IER)
options.B: Drafting Consensus Report (CR)
options.C: Approving CR

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: Both A) and C)

question: Which of the following is allowed by the Confidentiality clause:

options.A: Discuss evaluation matters with EU staff not involved in the evaluation
options.B: Contact partners in the consortium, sub-contractors or any third parties
options.C: Disclose names of your fellow experts.
options.D: Discuss evaluation matters with your fellow experts who are evaluating the same proposal in a consensus group or Panel review.

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: Discuss evaluation matters with your fellow experts who are evaluating the same proposal in a consensus group or Panel review.

question: Which of the following is NOT true with respect to the use of generative AI in proposal preparation:

options.A: It is not allowed
options.B: It is allowed, but the applicants must verify the accuracy, validity, and appropriateness of the content and any citations generated by the AI tool and correct any errors or inconsistencies.
options.C: It is allowed, but the applicants must provide a list of sources used to generate content and citations, including those generated by the AI tool. Double-check citations to ensure they are accurate and properly referenced.
options.D: It is allowed, but the applicants must be conscious of the potential for plagiarism where the AI tool may have reproduced substantial text from other sources. Check the original sources to be sure you are not plagiarising someone else’s work.
options.E: It is allowed, but the applicants must acknowledge the limitations of the AI tool in the proposal preparation, including the potential for bias, errors, and gaps in knowledge.

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: It is not allowed

question: Which of the following represent a possible Conflict of Interest (CoI) at proposal level (note: not exhaustive!):

options.A: I have collaborated in a research project with one of the applicants in 2021
options.B: I have published with one of the applicants in the past 3 years
options.C: I have heard of one of the applicants

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: I have published with one of the applicants in the past 3 years

question: I am automatically in a Conflict of Interest (CoI) at evaluation level if (note: not exhaustive!):

options.A: I am a director or trustee of the applicant
options.B: I have contributed to the drafting of a proposal submitted to the call
options.C: I am a National Contact Point
options.D: I am in one or more of the above cases

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: I am in one or more of the above cases

question: If I find out I might have a potential conflict of interest:

options.A: I flag this immediately to the Call Coordinator
options.B: I decline the assignment immediately
options.C: I continue with the evaluation as it is not my role to highlight it

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: I decline the assignment immediately

question: The Evaluation Workflow consists of:

options.A: Drafting IERs and quality check
options.B: Creating CR and reaching consensus
options.C: Cross reading and confirming the comments and scores

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: All A), B), and C)

question: The Vice Chairs Panellists get access for cross reading to

options.A: All proposals and their ESRs
options.B: Only to the ESRs of half of the proposals
options.C: Only to all above threshold proposals
options.D: Only to all proposals with a minority view from the individual evaluation
options.E: Only to the proposals with equal score

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: All proposals and their ESRs

question: When cross reading proposals and their ESR at their choice, the VCPs have to check for:

options.A: Consistency between comments and scores
options.B: Form an opinion about any cases of minority views, recorder during the evaluation
options.C: Apply the rules for tie resolution

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: A and B above

question: During the final Step 1 Panel the VCPs have to

options.A: Reevaluate the proposals they like
options.B: Confirm all comments and scores only for below-threshold proposals
options.C: Discuss and resolve any minority view cases
options.D: Priorities all proposals with equal scores
options.E: Discuss the categories of all above threshold proposals

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: Discuss and resolve any minority view cases

question: In preparation for the portfolio building process VCPs have to

options.A: Just read the Challenge guides
options.B: Assess the values of the various categories, defined in the Challenge guides, for the proposals allocated to them
options.C: Come up with new scores for proposals they want included in the final portfolio
options.D: Suggest lower scores for the proposals, which did not do self-assessment for the values of the categories relevant to them

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: Assess the values of the various categories, defined in the Challenge guides, for the proposals allocated to them

question: At Step 2 of the final Panel under the guidance f the Programme Manager the VCPs will

options.A: Discuss each (above-threshold) proposal in order to have a full and correct understanding of them within the whole group.
options.B: Confirm the values of the categories, as defined by the Challenge guide, of each proposal.
options.C: Discuss together the possible suitable portfolio of proposals by ranking them based on score and the portfolio considerations according to the portfolio building approach (as described in the Challenge guide).
options.D: In case it is considered necessary, propose minor adjustments to the proposals as far as needed for the consistency of the portfolio approach.

title: VCPs – Individual Evaluation and Portfolio Building
answerText: All of the above
